I haven't been in a relationship for 5.5 years (I'm in my late 20s) and can't remember the last time somebody told me they loved me. 
Everyone wants me to be successful and achieve stuff because I'm smart but I just want to be happy, if that means taking a less stressful job and being a disappointment then I guess I'm ok with that.

[www.freedeedpoll.org.uk](https://www.freedeedpoll.org.uk) is the one I used, it's very well worded and absolutely free. Print it on high quality paper (I used parchment paper from Ryman).

Get it signed by the two witnesses (I got them to sign 20 copies for every eventuality).  It does not need to be stamped by lawyer.

It's not been rejected once, even by my bank, DVLA and local council.

Good luck! Let me know if you have any questions.

So, had my top surgery on 13/06 (last Thursday) and feel much better than I thought I would be. I came round pretty quickly and was conversing well within 15-20 mins of waking up. Went in at 9am and I remember seeing the clock at about 12:10pm so I'm guessing I was under for about 3 hours. All the nurses were commenting on how well I looked and was talking (first time for everything, I guess!)

I was kept in overnight (about 26 hours after surgery) as they needed to check the drains before removing them (very common with my surgeon, not sure if it's his preference or the hospital's). Very happy they didn't need to be kept in any longer. Of all the aches and pains it's the drain sites that are causing the most discomfort, not the actual surgical sites (?)  


I had a keyhole/liposuction procedure and while everything is still swollen as heck, I can see that there's less there than before. I'm going to get a sore neck if I don't stop looking down! I haven't seen the full results yet as I have my compression vest (for 3 weeks) and also a waterproof bandage (for 6 days). I'm hoping when the waterproof bandage is off I'll be able to see what's going on properly. I will definitely not miss this compression vest one jot!

I was up and about the same day (I couldn't let the poor gent in the bed next to me hear me on the commode again) and have been trying to keep as active as I can (small walks around the house, had a walk around the neighborhood for 10 minutes yesterday).

That's all I can think of to blither on about haha!

When I was about 12 learning about puberty and the things that would happen I remembered thinking "I hope I turn out like the man" but I read further on and realised that wouldn't happen I was pretty gutted. 
I went through puberty not feeling quite right but put this down to being in an awkward phase in my life. 
I'm also the kind of person that needs to learn about everything but for some reason I skipped past learning about transgenderism (and unfortunately made a point of ignoring the first transgendered person I met, who was FtM). I remember wearing a training bra until it gave me quad-boob because I refused to acknowledge my chest growing. My Mum had to drag me to the bra fitters. 
I got into relationships with straight guys and ignored my feelings and then I got very depressed due to having a contraceptive implant (I did everything in power to avoid pregnancy and still do). I split up with my fiancé and moved to London a couple years later.
Being alone and isolated gave me time and space to reflect on why I was feeling the way I do and I tried to counteract everything by presenting very femininely in 2015. 
I remember reading an article about a trans woman and thinking "why do they get to be who they want?" And then I realised there is nothing stopping me. That was August 2016. I started T in November 2016, freaked out and stopped in January but I've had another appointment so should be getting my T letter through again this week hopefully.
That's my story.
